column1: # The shard table. THE one place a shard's identity lives; bash and Python both read this file.
# A "domain" to the router (src/retrieval/shard_router.py) is a CPC SUBCLASS, four characters.
# There are hundreds of those and there are eight shards, so a shard owns a PREFIX SET and the
# mapping subclass -> shard is by longest matching prefix. Every domain must land somewhere: the
# last row is the catch-all and is also where the always-emitted "unclassified" route goes, which
# is 1,024,320 publications, 20.6% of the corpus, that no classified shard can hold.
# The prefix sets are provisional. Workstream F builds the shard databases and owns how the corpus
# is actually cut; when F settles it, edit this file and nothing else. Rebalancing is a data move,
#   shard    shard id, also the label and the suffix of the VM name
#   prefixes comma separated CPC prefixes this shard owns, or * for the catch-all
# Only 03-transport exists today. See README.md for the one command that creates the rest and for
